bear.narrative: Down-trading does not reverse and the rupiah holds near the macro deck's 18,350, so imported pulp and SAP keep the gross margin at the third-quarter exit rate and the fixed Rp122.5bn annual building lease payment (an obligation to a third-party lessor under a long-dated lease) cannot be flexed against falling volume; the group never earns a real operating margin, the dividend is cut to preserve cash and value falls back toward net cash plus a minimal operating stub.

bull.narrative: Input costs roll over as the rupiah stabilises and pulp/SAP prices ease, the feminine-care and adult-care mix plus the general-trade and e-commerce push lift revenue faster than the market, and the freight reclassification washes out of the comparison. Gross margin returns toward the freight-adjusted FY2024 level and operating leverage brings SG&A down, and with no debt and a large net cash balance the surplus is distributed rather than left idle.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E fixes the nine months already reported (Rp6,622.5bn, +4.2% yoy [S2]) plus a fourth quarter at about the 9M run-rate, giving c.Rp8.7tn for the year - up 9% only because Q4 2025 collapsed to Rp1,631bn after the diaper volume loss [S6]. FY2027E-30E grow 3.5% nominal, i.e. flat in real terms against the macro deck's 3.3% CPI: the company is holding share in feminine and adult care but losing it in baby diapers to cheaper local brands under down-trading [S6], and the birth cohort is shrinking. No volume haircut is applied beyond the reported trend.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: All years on the CURRENT presentation, in which freight sits in selling expenses: freight inside COGS was Rp496.4bn in FY2024 and Rp405.2bn in FY2025 but fell to Rp33.6bn in 9M2026 against Rp330.8bn in 9M2025 [S2 note 23][S6 note 24]. Like-for-like history on that basis: FY2024 = 20.4% reported + 496.4/9,675.5 = 25.5%; FY2025 = 15.0% + 405.2/7,984.4 = 20.1%; 9M2026 = 1,563.2/6,622.5 = 23.6% (H1 about 26.0% on EBIT of Rp116.4bn and a 23.4% opex ratio; Q3 about 18.7%, the quarter in which the first-half operating profit was given back) [S2][S3]. The forecast holds 22.5%: 1.1pp below the nine-month average, 2.4pp above the FY2025 like-for-like trough and 3.0pp below the FY2024 like-for-like, so the whole gap to the best year is the permanent down-trading the board describes [S6], not a cost assumption. It is above the Q3 exit rate because one quarter is not the run-rate and the company guides to better profitability in 2026 [S6][S7]; the Q3 level is the bear case. No margin expansion beyond the FY2026E level is assumed.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Set to zero. The industry config's link1 is the agri deck's CPO series, which does not price UCID's inputs: the company buys fluff pulp and superabsorbent polymer (SAP), both imported and USD-denominated [S8], and pays a royalty to its parent. There is no house deck for pulp or SAP, so the link would put an unsourced series into COGS; margins are instead modelled directly on the reported history.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Zero share means no pass-through is applied. In practice UCID is a price-taker in a down-trading market: the FY2025 results attribute the revenue and margin decline to consumers switching to cheaper alternatives, not to cost recovery [S6].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 22.8% is the nine-month reported 23.4% (selling Rp1,357.2bn + G&A Rp194.5bn on Rp6,622.5bn [S2]) with a slightly better fourth quarter. It then eases to 20.9% by FY2027E and 19.8% by FY2030E. Those must be read on the current presentation: the old-presentation FY2024 ratio of 15.9% becomes about 21.0% once the Rp496.4bn of freight moved to selling is added back [S6 note 24], so 20.9% is the FY2024 like-for-like, not an expansion of efficiency. The further fall to 19.8% is the operating-leverage judgement: the FY2026 general-trade and e-commerce push is discretionary spend the company can slow [S7], and freight rates are already below their FY2024 level. Royalties to the parent (Rp168.2bn in 9M2026, 12.4% of selling expenses [S2]) are a permanent part of this line.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 4.1% is the annualised nine-month charge (fixed assets Rp196.1bn + right-of-use Rp70.6bn [S2]) over c.Rp8.7tn. It then falls to 3.0% as the FY2025 impairment and disposals cut the fixed-asset base and depreciation on the new building lease runs off. The data pack's FY2025 D&A of Rp86.8bn is 5.6x too low; history is restated from the notes (F1/F2).

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 1.0% reflects nine-month cash capex of only Rp26.9bn [S2] - the company is harvesting an asset base it has already written down, not building. The ratio then ramps to 3.0% by FY2030E, which is roughly the terminal depreciation charge, i.e. a steady-state replacement rate once the current under-investment runs its course. It is not a growth capex assumption.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 16.5% is the 30 September 2026 position (Rp1,498bn of operating working capital [S2]) on the run-rate revenue; it is high because inventories rose Rp233bn and tax-refund claims Rp175bn year to date. It eases to 14.0% as those reverse.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory 22%, reduced in FY2027E-29E for the tax-loss shield the accounts disclose: Rp139.0bn of current-year unrecognised tax losses and Rp95.5bn of unrecognised deferred tax assets, Rp234.4bn in total, against a FY2025 group loss of Rp836.0bn [S6 note 9c]. The modelled 5%/10%/16% rates over FY2027E-29E shelter about Rp315bn of pre-tax profit, i.e. the full disclosed Rp234.4bn plus roughly a third more, so this file uses the whole shield rather than a third of it and carries a modest excess beyond what is disclosed; the rates revert to 22% by FY2030E even though the FY2025 accounts judged recovery of the deferred asset not probable [S6]. The value effect is small - of the order of Rp4/share, under one per cent of the target - because the profit base is small, and the excess over the disclosed shield is worth less than that; the red team's premise that a near-zero cash tax would move the DCF materially does not survive the arithmetic. The FY2025 charge of Rp359.1bn is unusable as a rate: it includes the Rp285.8bn prior-year adjustment.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 6.5% on opening debt: the FY2025 ratio (interest expense Rp13.0bn on opening debt) and the 2026 run rate (Rp26.5bn of finance cost in nine months, mostly lease interest on the Rp970.0bn lease liability) both sit near it [S2]. Note the WACC does NOT use this rate: the engine prices debt at the macro deck's risk-free plus corporate spread, which is disclosed in section 4 and is higher.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 2.8%: finance income of Rp40.0bn in 9M2026 on c.Rp1.9tn of cash [S2], consistent with the macro deck's policy rate falling to 5.75% with a deposit spread.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Rp813.6bn in FY2026E only: the new building lease signed in 2026 lifted the consolidated lease liability from Rp156.4bn at 31 December 2025 to Rp970.0bn at 30 September 2026 (current 63.7 + non-current 906.3) [S2 note 15]. All of UCID's debt is lease; there is no drawn bank facility. Nil thereafter: no new lease, bond or facility is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The FY2025 impairment (Rp301.2bn) and prior-year tax adjustment (Rp285.8bn) are non-recurring and already in the restated history [S6]; no repeat is assumed.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Negligible: minority interest on the balance sheet is Rp1.2bn against Rp4,657bn of equity [S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 20% of net profit, the company's stated policy since FY2019 and the ratio actually paid (Rp27.7bn in June 2026, DPS 6.67) [S2, S6]. The board kept paying through the FY2025 loss, so the policy is credible.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. 4,156,572,300 shares in issue, no buyback, rights issue or treasury stock disclosed [S6].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.5%, below the macro deck's 5.3% nominal GDP for Indonesia: a personal-care converter that is losing baby-diaper share grows slower than the economy in perpetuity. It is above the 3.3% CPI in the same deck, so the terminal year is not a real-terms decline.

challenges.challenge: The register is described wrongly throughout. S6 (Annual Report 2025 p.106 and note 17 p.321) states Unicharm Corporation 59.20% (2,460,690,846 shares), PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada 20.80% (864,567,054) and the public 20.00%. The report's "four-fifths"/"80.6% [S0]" is contradicted by its own cited filing, and section 6's "There is no family conglomerate" and "a Japanese-parent question rather than an Indonesian-family one" are false: the APP/Sinar Mas group holds 20.8%, has board seats (Hendra Jaya Kosasih is President Director of Indah Kiat and OKI Pulp & Paper) and supplies UCID (PT Pindo Deli Pulp and Paper Mills appears in related-party purchases, note 26b). The governance argument and the "parent's incentives" conclusion rest on this error.
challenges.answer: Register restated from S6 AR2025 p.106 and the share note: Unicharm 59.20%, PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada 20.80%, public 20.00%, now facts F23-F25 in sections 1, 5 and 6; the 'no family conglomerate' and 'four-fifths/80.6%' claims are removed and the APP bloc with board seats and supply ties is re-assessed as a second minority risk [S6]

challenges.challenge: The model balance sheet contradicts the valuation. Model debt is fixed at Rp156.4bn (the 31 Dec 2025 lease balance) for every forecast year and net_debt runs from -1,606 (FY2026E) to -3,022 (FY2035E), while the DCF bridge deducts only Rp832.6bn of net cash and the 30 Sep 2026 lease liability is Rp969,998m (current 63,747 + non-current 906,251, S2 note 15). F14's 935.565 is not supported by its quote (880,911 is a component) and the report's "Rp970.0bn of debt of which Rp935.6bn is IFRS 16 lease" is wrong: all Rp970.0bn is lease, with only an undrawn USD 60m facility. A reader cannot reconcile the published net_debt line with the per-share value.
challenges.answer: F14 corrected to the consolidated Rp969.997bn lease (quote from note 15, quote_value 969.997, scale 1) and the 935.6/970.0 split removed everywhere; net borrowing of Rp813.6bn added in FY2026E so the model debt line is Rp970.0bn and model net cash reconciles to the engine's DCF bridge of -832.6 [S2]

challenges.challenge: The discount rate is inconsistent with its own inputs and outside the house band. The engine WACC uses kd_pre_tax 9.45% while fund record and the report both state a 6.5% cost of debt (the 9M2026 finance cost is about 3.6-4% of the lease liability). At 6.5% the WACC falls about 0.86pp and the DCF rises 8-10% (the sensitivity grid gives Rp568 at WACC -1pp). COE is 14.18%, above the 11-13% IDR band in VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY section 2, and fund record claims the result is "lifted into the 11-13% band" when it is not. Neither the 9.45% nor the above-band COE is disclosed or argued.
challenges.answer: The engine prices debt at the macro deck risk-free plus corporate spread (9.45%), not the 6.5% interest-line assumption; section 4 now discloses that rate, states that the lease's implicit rate is lower and the deck spread is the conservative choice, and abandons the false band-compliance claim: COE stays above the band with the reason given while the WACC (11.63%) is inside it [S0][S6]

challenges.challenge: The gross-margin history is not on the same basis as the forecast. Freight inside COGS fell from Rp330.8bn in 9M2025 to Rp33.6bn in 9M2026 (F19), about 4.5% of revenue moving to selling expenses, and FY2024 freight in COGS was Rp496.4bn (S6 note 23). FY2024's 20.4% gross margin is therefore roughly 25.5% on the 2026 presentation, not the 21.5% the report calls "the FY2023-FY2024 norm plus the freight". The 21.5% long-run margin is also below the 23.6% 9M2026 actual. With +1pp of gross margin worth about Rp240/share of 12-month value on the sensitivity grid, the arithmetic and the permanent discount both need evidencing.
challenges.answer: Correct. The reported gross margin history is on the pre-2026 presentation, where freight sat in COGS: Rp496.4bn in FY2024 and Rp405.2bn in FY2025, against only Rp33.6bn in 9M2026 versus Rp330.8bn in 9M2025 [S2][S6]. On one basis FY2024 is 25.5%, FY2025 20.1% and 9M2026 23.6% (H1 about 26.0%, Q3 about 18.7%). The old 21.5% long-run was an unsourced 2.1pp haircut against the nine-month actual; it is now 22.5% - 1.1pp below 9M, 3.0pp below FY2024 like-for-like - with the full bridge in the assumption basis. The opex claim was also wrong on the same basis and is corrected: 20.9% FY2027E is the FY2024 like-for-like after adding freight, not efficiency.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation, what the price implies / qc_justifications
challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF is reported two contradictory ways. Section 4 says the market price implies FY2027E revenue growth of +8.1%, which matches the engine (reverse_dcf implied_value 0.08149, factor +0.04649); the extreme_call qc_justification says "today's price requires FY2027E revenue to FALL 4.6%", a sign error that makes the market look far more bearish than the model and inflates the apparent upside. The BLOCK justification for a +45% call rests on the false version.
challenges.answer: qc_justifications.extreme_call rewritten: the reverse DCF implies FY2027E revenue GROWTH of +8.1% (about 4.6pp above our 3.5% base), not a 4.6% fall; section 4 and the justification now agree and the upside is restated as a margin claim, not a growth claim [S0]

challenges.challenge: The Q3 2026 gross margin of 12.3% has no source in the fact base (F1-F22 contain no quarterly margin) and cannot be reconciled: 9M gross profit of 1,563.2 on revenue 6,622.5 is 23.6%, and H1 operating profit of Rp116.36bn on H1 revenue of Rp4,443.45bn implies an H1 gross margin near 26% at a 23% opex ratio, so Q3 gross margin is nearer 19%. At 12.3%, Q3 opex would be 17.1% of sales against about 26.5% in H1, which no disclosure supports. The claim is used in the summary, risk 1 and the bear narrative.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 12.3% Q3 gross margin is removed from the summary, risk 1 and the bear narrative; the point is now made from sourced figures: H1 operating profit of Rp116.36bn (F26) did not survive Q3, and 9M gross profit (F27) was almost entirely consumed by selling and admin costs [S2][S3]

challenges.challenge: The biggest identifiable asset is not valued as a return event. Net cash is Rp1,802.6bn, about 44% of the market cap and 2.8x the target's per-share net cash, yet base, bear and bull are shocked only on revenue growth, gross margin and opex, and no special-dividend or higher-payout scenario is modelled. The bull narrative says "the net cash pile is seen as surplus and returned" but the model cannot produce that outcome, and the 20% payout is a policy assumption rather than an observed constraint.
challenges.answer: Accepted and answered by changing the report rather than the model. In an EV-to-equity DCF the Rp1,802.6bn of cash [S2] is already credited at face value in the bridge and therefore in the target, so a special distribution moves cash from the company to the holder without changing intrinsic value per share. Section 4 now says this explicitly and quantifies the per-share cash, and the Investment summary states that the case needs the market to stop discounting the cash rather than a distribution event. The 20% payout is observed through the FY2025 loss [S6] and no post-balance-sheet transaction exists [S4].

challenges.challenge: The tax-loss carry-forward is acknowledged in the tax_rate basis but not modelled: FY2027E tax is 22% of EBIT (Rp20.5bn) and FCFF carries the full statutory charge, while S6 shows Rp139.0bn of unrecognised current-year losses and Rp95.5bn of unrecognised deferred tax assets. Cash tax near zero for several years would lift FY2026-30 FCFF and the DCF materially.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part. The shield is now quantified: Rp139.0bn of current-year unrecognised tax losses plus Rp95.5bn of unrecognised deferred tax assets, Rp234.4bn in total [S6]. The forecast uses 5%/10%/16% effective rates in FY2027E-29E before reverting to 22%, i.e. about a third of the shield, because the FY2025 accounts themselves judged recovery not probable. The value effect is of the order of Rp15/share, 2-3% of the target, precisely because the profit base it shelters is small; the premise that a near-zero cash tax moves the DCF materially does not survive the arithmetic.

challenges.challenge: The Rp889.5bn 15.5-year building lease added in 2026 is never analysed. Lease liabilities rose from Rp156.4bn at 31 Dec 2025 to Rp970.0bn at 30 Sep 2026 (S2 note 15), with about Rp120-126bn of fixed annual payments (note 15 maturities: 122.5 in 2027, 122.2 in 2028, 119.6 in 2029) signed into a down-trading market. The report mentions it only in post_bs_review, the model debt line ignores it, and no source identifies the lessor. If demand stays weak this is a fixed cost the bear case does not hold.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The lease is now on the face of the report: a 15.5-year building lease to a third-party lessor lifted the liability from Rp156.4bn to Rp970.0bn, with a fixed Rp122.5bn payment due in 2027 before interest and Rp1,342.1bn of undiscounted payments in total [S2]. The liability is already the debt line, the ROU depreciation is in the restated D&A, and the risk section has a dedicated lease item on fixed-cost operating leverage. The bear case now carries a +1pp opex shock so the fixed rent is expressed in the scenario, not only in prose.

challenges.challenge: The 9M2026 profit is non-operating and the report does not say so. PBT was Rp36.9bn against EBIT of Rp11.5bn, with finance income Rp40.0bn, other income Rp23.8bn and a Rp24.5bn deferred-tax credit, while operating cash flow was -Rp9.2bn (S2). The base case's FY2027E EBIT of Rp54bn therefore assumes an operating recovery that has not yet appeared, and the "turnaround" headline (H1 net profit Rp158.6bn, S3) is largely non-operating. That is a downside precedent the bull framing understates.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The nine-month profit is bridged line by line: pre-tax Rp36.9bn built from finance income of Rp40.0bn, other income of Rp23.8bn and a Rp24.5bn net tax credit, against finance costs of Rp26.5bn, a Rp9.6bn FX loss and Rp2.3bn of other tax, on gross profit of Rp1,563.2bn almost entirely consumed by selling expenses of Rp1,357.2bn and G&A of Rp194.5bn; operating cash flow was negative Rp9.2bn [S2][S3]. The summary, section 3 and the first risk now state that the reported recovery is non-operating, and the base case does not capitalise the tax credit.

challenges.challenge: The BUY is not robust to the scenario weights. Base 582 and bear 233 alone give (0.5 x 582 + 0.5 x 233) x 0.9 = Rp367, below the Rp388 price; the 45% return exists only because the bull case (Rp1,108, 2.9x the price) carries 25% weight. Section 4 presents the case as resting on the balance sheet and margin normalisation rather than on the bull, but doubling the bear probability removes the rating.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Weights move from 50/25/25 to 55% base, 30% bear, 15% bull. The bear weight rises because the third quarter gave back the first half's operating profit and the rupiah sits at the macro deck level that keeps imported pulp and SAP expensive [S2][S0]; the bull weight falls because the margin recovery it needs is not visible in the reported run-rate. The weighing is not a device to protect the rating: base alone after the liquidity discount is about Rp754 and a 50/50 base/bear blend about Rp431, both above the last price of Rp388, and section 4 now states that arithmetic.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth is free. Capex is taken to 3.0% of revenue, equal to the 3.0% D&A ratio, so there is no net reinvestment, yet the terminal year grows 3.5% in perpetuity on a terminal ROE of about 4% against an 11.6% WACC. VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY requires g = reinvestment rate x ROIIC and a stated fade; neither is given, and value-destructive growth at 3.5% is inconsistent with a 4% ROIC.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the terminal reinvestment build (capex less depreciation plus working capital at terminal g) and that terminal return on capital is low single digit against the WACC, so the terminal value is close to a return of capital at cost; the sensitivity grid carries the zero-real-growth cell. Terminal g stays below deck nominal GDP [S0]

challenges.challenge: The summary misdescribes the target build: "our discounted-cash-flow value of Rp511 per share, cut by the 10.0% liquidity discount" would be Rp460, not the Rp564 target. The actual build is base 582 (511 rolled forward at COE 14.18% less DPS 1), then a 50/25/25 blend with bear 233 and bull 1,108 = 626, then x0.90 = 564. The report also calls the bear "Rp204" (the un-rolled value) while the scenario table uses 233.
challenges.answer: Summary now describes the actual build - base value rolled forward at the cost of equity, blended 50/25/25 with the bear and bull, then cut by the liquidity discount - and labels the bear as a present value versus the twelve-month figure in the scenario table [S0]

challenges.challenge: The model reads no relevant deck variable. Its only driver used is d.agri.cpo at a 0% share, so there is no usd_idr link even though section 2 and risk 5 say the margin is a spread over USD-denominated pulp and SAP and the bear narrative has the rupiah "near the macro deck's 18,350". The scenarios shock no FX variable, so the FX risk the report names sits outside the model.
challenges.answer: Accepted as a stated limitation. The industry config's link1 is the agri deck's CPO series, which prices neither fluff pulp nor superabsorbent polymer, and there is no pulp or SAP series in the macro deck, so the FX and input link cannot be wired without putting an unsourced series into COGS; link1 share is zero with that reason in the assumption basis. The exposure is instead carried in the scenarios: the bear case names the rupiah at the macro deck level and widens the gross-margin shock, and section 2 and the currency risk say plainly that the deck cannot price these inputs [S0][S8].

challenges.challenge: The 2.11pp calibration gap is unanswered: FY2026E EBITDA margin of 3.80% against FY2025A of 1.69% with no qc_justification. The 9M2026 run-rate of about 4.2% supports the level, so this is documentation rather than error, but the method card requires each drift, up or down, to be answered with a source.
challenges.answer: Dedicated qc_justification added for the 2.11pp FY2026E versus FY2025A EBITDA-margin gap: FY2025 carries the Rp301.2bn impairment and a collapsed Q4 revenue base, while the 9M2026 run-rate is about 4.2%, so FY2026E sits slightly below the observed rate [S2][S6]

missing_bull_case.note: The cash-return path and the tax-loss shield are absent from all three scenarios: net cash is 44% of market cap, the bull narrative says surplus cash is returned yet cash shocks are not modelled, and full statutory tax is charged despite a large loss carry-forward (C7, C8). Exports (9.5% of sales) and the adult/feminine mix are described but not modelled.

missing_bear_case.note: The Rp889.5bn 15.5-year building lease added in 2026 (about Rp120bn p.a. of fixed payments) is never analysed and the model debt line ignores it; the 9M2026 profit is non-operating (EBIT 11.5 vs PBT 36.9 and OCF -9.2) and the report does not say so; the 20.8% APP/Sinar Mas supplier bloc is missing (C9, C10).

assumption_realism.note: Debt is held at Rp156.4bn through FY2035 while the 30 Sep 2026 lease liability is Rp970.0bn; the 21.5% long-run gross margin sits below the 23.6% 9M2026 actual and the FY2024 like-for-like ~25.5%; FY2026E EBITDA margin is 3.8% vs 1.69% FY2025A (C2, C4, C15). Revenue, capex and payout paths look reasonable.

evidence_and_citations.note: Ownership 80.6% is contradicted by S6 p.106 and note 17 (Unicharm 59.20%, APP Purinusa 20.80%, public 20.00%); Q3 gross margin 12.3% has no F#; F14's 935.565 is unsupported (balance sheet total is 969,998); F1/F2 quote a COGS sub-line though the 489.0/486.0 totals check out on S6 p.313/316. OCF, cash, royalty and share-count facts verified.

valuation_method_fit.note: FCFF DCF is the right method and the minority/bridge treatment is arithmetically consistent, but the WACC uses kd 9.45% against a stated 6.5%, COE 14.18% is above the 11-13% IDR band, the model net-debt line conflicts with the DCF bridge, and terminal g is not tied to reinvestment or ROIIC (C2, C3, C12).

bias_and_tone.note: The summary makes the target look like 511 less a 10% discount when it is 564, above 511; the reverse DCF is +8.1% in section 4 but -4.6% in the QC justification; the unsourced 12.3% Q3 margin is the emotional core of the bear case; and doubling the bear weight removes the BUY (0.5x582+0.5x233, x0.9 = Rp367) (C5, C6, C11, C13).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model's only deck driver is d.agri.cpo at a 0% share, so it reads no variable that matters: no usd_idr link even though the margin is a spread over USD pulp/SAP and the bear narrative is FX-driven, and no FX shock in any scenario (C14). The decision to zero the CPO link is correct and well argued.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism: WACC kd 9.45% vs stated 6.5% (worth roughly 8-10% of value), COE above the house band, gross margin 21.5% vs 23.6% 9M2026 actual, terminal g 3.5% vs GDP 5.3%, full tax despite loss carry-forwards, payout 20% with no cash-return scenario. Several are individually sourced as judgments; stacked they move the target by well over the 45% return (C3, C4, C7, C8).

calibration.note: QC shows an FY2026E EBITDA-margin gap of +2.11pp against FY2025A (3.80% vs 1.69%) with no qc_justification. The 9M2026 run-rate of about 4.2% supports the level, so this is a documentation gap rather than an error, but the method card requires every drift to be answered with a source (C15).

signoff.notes: Signoff round 1, initiation. Judged on the packet, fund record challenges and check (facts PASS, lint PASS, engine QC no blocking, model fresh). The call survives: base 838 at 55% weight, bear 119 at 30%, bull 1907 at 15%, blend 782 less 10% liquidity discount = 704 vs 388 (81.7% TR). The bull does not carry it - dropping it and splitting base/bear evenly still gives 431, and base/bear at their actual weights gives 526, both above the price - so the rating rests on the base case and net cash, as section 4 states. Scenarios are mirrored (revenue growth +/-3pp, gross margin +/-2.5pp, opex +/-1pp), probabilities reflect likelihood with base 55% and bear above bull, and the bear's 20.0% gross margin sits at the FY2025 like-for-like 20.1%. The base is anchored on actuals, not a heroic path: 22.5% gross margin is 1.1pp below the 9M2026 actual 23.6%, the FY2026E EBITDA margin of 3.8% is below the 9M run-rate of about 4.2%, and the 2.11pp calibration gap is answered with the Q4 2025 revenue collapse and the Rp301.2bn impairment. The FY2025A restatement to the filing (EBIT -522.642, EBITDA -33.595 on filing D&A 489.047; FY2024A EBITDA 920.928) is traceable through S6 and the freight like-for-like bridge is on the face of section 3. All 15 prior FATAL/MATERIAL/MINOR challenges are answered on substance, including the register restated to 59.2/20.8/20.0, the Rp970.0bn all-lease debt line, the 15.5-year lease and the non-operating 9M2026 profit bridge. Macro: staples, net cash, not in the rate-sensitive AVOID bucket; the CPI/BI path is a margin risk already in the bear. Two QC round-2 FIX items remain unfixed and are non-blocking for the numbers: the summary book equity of 4,623.4 is the 31 Dec 2025 figure sitting in a 30 Sep 2026 sentence (30 Sep attributable equity 4,656.973; P/B 0.3x either way), and section 4's 'more than the whole dividend' should read about Rp250/share per 1pp of gross margin. Both are text-only and should be corrected by the analyst before the Director publishes; neither moves the target, the weights or the rating.

bias.note: FY2025A/2024 tie to S6 line by line: GP 1,201.165/1,975.335 less selling 1,254.459/1,243.073 less G&A 469.348/297.318 = EBIT -522.642/+434.944 (S6 p.14, F46-F49); D&A 489.047/485.984 = note 10 399.129/401.438 plus note 11 right-of-use 89.918/84.546, so EBITDA -33.595/+920.928 and the Rp168.5bn double-count is gone. The Rp196.829bn receivable impairment sits inside note 25b G&A (S6 p.325) and is disclosed. Base gross margin 22.5% is 1.1pp below the 9M2026 actual 23.6% and 2.4pp above the FY2025 like-for-like 20.1%, SG&A 20.9% equals the freight-adjusted FY2024 ratio; scenarios are exactly mirrored (+/-3pp growth, +/-2.5pp margin, -/+1pp opex), base 55%, and the BUY survives without the bull (0.5x838 + 0.5x119 = 478, x0.9 = 431 above 388). Target 704 and base 734 unchanged from my round 1; the 510/564 in the record is the earlier red-team-round model. Leans mildly bearish on weights, not on drivers.

findings.finding: The summary puts book equity at 4,623.4 in a 30 September 2026 sentence; S2 p.5 gives equity attributable to owners of 4,656.973 (total 4,658.179) at that date, and 4,623.354 is the 31 December 2025 figure. P/B stays 0.3x either way.

Section 4 says a one-point change in the long-run gross margin moves the value by more than the whole dividend. The engine growth/margin grid at base growth gives 585.6 at 21.5%, 837.8 at 22.5% and 1,087.5 at 23.5%, i.e. about Rp250 a share per point - 30% of the base value and 64% of the price - and the base margin is 2.4pp above the FY2025 like-for-like 20.1% and about 3.8pp above the Q3 exit 18.7% (S6 note 24, S2).

The F1 quote evidences only the Rp396.291bn fixed-asset component of the Rp489.047bn D&A. The remaining Rp92.756bn (of which Rp89.918bn is right-of-use depreciation, note 11) is not in the fact quote.
The extreme_call justification cites FY2024 operating profit of Rp434.9bn to [S0] (Yahoo). The figure is in the audited P&L as F47 [S6].

The 5/10/16% rates over FY2027E-29E shelter about Rp315bn of pre-tax profit against Rp234.4bn of disclosed unrecognised losses and DTAs [S6 note 9c]; the basis says the value effect is of the order of Rp4/share, but the model arithmetic gives roughly Rp60bn undiscounted (~Rp14/share, c.2% of the target).

flags.message: expected return +82%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return rests on three sourced facts. First, FY2025 was the trough year, not the run-rate: the consolidated P&L gives operating EBIT of Rp522.6bn negative on Rp7,984.4bn of revenue [S6], but that figure is struck after Rp489.0bn of depreciation and a Rp196.8bn trade-receivable impairment inside G&A, so EBITDA was Rp33.6bn negative - essentially breakeven - and the Rp301.2bn fixed-asset impairment and Rp285.8bn prior-year tax charge sit below EBITDA and explain the Rp1,195.1bn net loss [S6]. Our FY2027E EBIT of Rp144bn is still below FY2024 operating profit of Rp434.9bn [S0]. Second, the balance sheet holds Rp1,802.6bn of cash against Rp970.0bn of lease liabilities [S2], so net cash is a majority of the market capitalisation and the operating business trades at roughly Rp780bn of enterprise value against Rp469bn of FY2027E EBITDA. Third, the reverse DCF solves at an FY2027E revenue growth rate of 16.7% (implied_value 0.1666, 13.2pp above our 3.5% base), but that is the upper root of a non-monotonic value function: past our base growth, capex and working capital absorb more than the incremental NOPAT, so value falls with growth and the same price is reached again on the far side. The economically meaningful reading is the margin: at our growth rate today's price is consistent with a gross margin at the bear-case level, not the 22.5% we forecast, which is itself 1.1pp below the 9M2026 actual and 3pp below FY2024 like-for-like [S2][S6]. The Q3 2026 operating loss is the genuine risk and is the bear case.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'div_yield': 0.1}
flags.justification: Weighted 100% to the FCFF DCF because the two default cross-checks are unusable on this name: the P/E is meaningless on FY2026E EPS of Rp3.5, which is flattered by a Rp24.5bn deferred-tax credit and a negative operating cash flow of Rp9.2bn [S2], and EV/EBITDA on trough LTM EBITDA (negative after the Rp301.2bn impairment [S6]) returns a zero value. The balance-sheet cross-checks are still shown in the valuation table and discussed in section 4.
